# IvritSuite Improvement Log

The memory of the continuous-improvement loop. **Read this first every session.** One concern per
iteration, one commit per iteration. Prioritization: P1 (data loss/security/broken core/export
corruption) > P2 (silently wrong output/undo holes/a11y blockers) > P3 (perf/dead UI/confusing
copy/consistency) > P4 (polish). Tie-breakers: (1) affects teachers' saved work, (2) affects the
printed/exported artifact a student receives, (3) dual-audience (Hebrew + secular) wins, (4) smallest diff.

## Candidates (prioritized, top = next)

Two consequences: (1) **cross-origin requests bypass the service worker (CLAUDE.md, Service Worker section), so the logo cannot work offline in an installed PWA** -- the footer renders a broken-image icon beside the alt text, which is exactly the "does this page look cared for" question pass M exists to ask; (2) a `files.readme.io/<hash>-image.png` URL is an ephemeral doc-host asset path that can rot at any time, taking the attribution mark with it. **The suite already has the opposite convention written down: the Starting Fonts intake vendors partner assets as "vendored same-origin copies, never hotlinked".** Fix = vendor both PNGs next to the other static media, repoint the two `<img>`, drop `files.readme.io` from both CSPs, and (optionally) precache them. **HONEST BLOCKER: this container's egress proxy returns HTTP 403 (CONNECT tunnel failed) for `files.readme.io`, so live reachability could not be verified and the bytes could not be downloaded here. A session with working egress -- or the maintainer dropping the two files in -- can finish this in one small commit.** Attribution wording is Sefaria's credit line, so if any visible text changes it is **gate 2**; swapping the image source alone is not.

- [ ] P4 (**NEW S263 iter 5** -- a METHOD finding that RETRACTED a P2 this session had already half-written against itself; the most reusable thing the run produced) | pass M / C / N protocol | **A pixel-sampling contrast probe measures the brightest ANTIALIASED pixel, and therefore under-reports a THIN glyph under `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased`.** The dashboard's fullscreen exit ✕ measured 2.98:1 light / 3.77:1 dark on a page whose CSS is provably correct (plate 0.72, no group opacity, `#fff`, opacity 1) -- the page that FIXED this very pattern at S248. Group opacity, ancestor `filter`/`mix-blend`/`isolation`, `backdrop-filter` and plate translucency were each ruled out by forcing them off; the brightest pixel in the glyph box stayed `rgb(110,113,121)` even over an opaque black plate. **Cause: the dashboard sets `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased` page-wide while torah and the generator resolve `auto`; everything else about the glyph is byte-equal (Arial, 24px, w400, `#fff`, same 20x27 ink box, same U+2715).** `antialiased` drops subpixel rendering and renders thin strokes lighter, so peak coverage is ~43%, not 100%. **RULE: a low contrast reading on a thin stroke is not a finding until a shape-aware or visual check agrees.** Corollary, and the reason this did not invalidate the sibling fix: iteration 3's generator numbers moved 1.78 -> 7.95 on the SAME probe, SAME page, SAME `auto` smoothing, with before/after crops showing a ghost becoming a solid plate -- a delta measured against itself is trustworthy where an absolute threshold across pages is not.

Do not migrate it to `dvh`.** S260's viewport-unit census named it the suite's highest-consequence `100vh` carrier, on the general rule that `100vh` exceeds the visible viewport while a phone's URL bar is expanded. That rule does not reach this declaration: **`body.fullscreen` is applied ONLY by the `fullscreenchange` listener**, so the rule is evaluated only while the document is in real Fullscreen — where the browser chrome is hidden and `100vh` IS the visible viewport. On iOS Safari element fullscreen is unsupported, `requestFullscreen().catch(() => {})` swallows the rejection, and `body.fullscreen` never applies at all. Either way the declaration is never live while collapsing chrome is on screen. Same standing as `body{min-height:100vh}` on 11 pages: **correct, and a future sweep must leave it alone.** `.app{min-height: calc(100vh - 72px)}` is a min-height floor and is likewise fine. What REMAINS of the S260 census: the ~13 modal `max-height:NNvh` sites, and the `.hk-panel` trio blocked inside the byte-identical shared keyboard block. | found: 2026-08-26, S262

Both were caught only by dispatching real keys and reading `document.activeElement` across five presses. | found: 2026-08-26, S259

The generator's `aside#appSidebar.sidebar` is untouched and unattributed.

**The one dimension a byte check cannot clear produced all 3 findings — "do the claims still match what the tool does".** The copy is byte-identical; the UI beneath it moved 3,538 lines. All three were gate-2 approved and **all three shipped this session** (3237da8): FM's HowTo naming 3 of the wizard's 4 sources (Drawing mode absent) under a step still called "Upload your letters"; the dashboard's Schedule Sync answer describing "a preset and an end time to each period" — precisely the single-day format the tool now calls "your existing schedule" and offers to migrate into the weekly grid; and the dictionary's filter list omitting Browse by Theme.
**The scope discovery that mattered:** each JSON-LD claim has a **VISIBLE FAQ twin** on the same page, and every twin carried the *identical* stale wording in **both languages** — so the structured data was never diverging from the page; the page had fallen behind the tool. Fixing only the JSON-LD would have manufactured a fresh JSON-LD↔visible mismatch, worse than either, so both halves moved together (3 JSON-LD claims + 3 localized EN/HE strings, worded to agree).
**⚑ This REVISES a convention S142's L run ratified.** That run saw the same shape and wrote "newer features like dictionary themes / torah copy simply aren't enumerated, nothing claimed is stale" — i.e. non-enumeration is not staleness. S190 narrows it: a **closed enumeration that asserts the complete set** ("one per image, a full sheet, or an existing font file") IS stale once the set grows, and a description of *how a feature works* that no longer describes it (the dashboard) was never non-enumeration at all. Merely incomplete prose still isn't a hit. The dictionary item is the one S142 explicitly declined; it shipped this time because the maintainer chose all three at gate 2.

Contract fixed BEFORE measuring, five dimensions: **PRESENT** (visible in-flight text) · **ANNOUNCED** (in a live region) · **CLEARS-OK** · **CLEARS-FAIL** (replaced by an error, never left as "Loading…") · **GUARDED** (no stacked re-fire). (2) torah_trainer appeared to show **no** busy text — **a harness fault**: a `waitForFunction` on `#ttParshaSelect option` (that select has no direct `option` children) burned the entire in-flight window before the first sample.

_(**S191 Pass C** — accessibility, one tool: **`torah_trainer.html`**, the S190 pointer's strongly-favored target and its 4th dedicated C (S18 → S72 → S146 → S191). The point of the pick was the three interactive surfaces added since S146 that had never had a dedicated audit — the S190 sticky bulk dock, the S188 type-a-range verse picker, the copy bar — and **the pick paid: 2 of the 3 findings that shipped were defects in the bulk dock itself, one of them a P2.** Structurally the page remains very strong: 124 visible controls with 0 naming defects in either language, 64-stop tab order in a sensible region sequence, a clean drawer focus-trap/Escape/restore contract, 20/20 visible focus rings in both themes, 0 pageerrors everywhere.)_
**The method lesson of the run: the two loudest automated signals were both wrong, and both would have been logged by a less suspicious pass.** (1) "35 of 64 tab stops have no focus indicator" — Chromium computes its own UA focus ring as `outline: <color> auto 0px`, so **`getComputedStyle().outlineWidth` cannot detect a focus ring at all**; a screenshot pixel-diff refuted it 20/20 in both themes. Any future C run that reads styles for this is measuring nothing. (2) "6 tab stops are invisible (0×0)" — those are the toggle-switch `<input>`s, deliberately hidden behind their `.slider`, which the existing `input:focus-visible + .slider` rule rings correctly. **A third near-miss on the verification side:** the fix-verification harness reported the gold **Copy All** button at 1:1 because an opaque `rgb()` parses to 3 components, so an `alpha > 0` guard is `false` for it and every solid-background element gets measured against its ancestor's plate instead of its own fill. The guard must be `alpha === undefined || alpha > 0`.
**And the injection lesson, which cost the first three probe runs:** `currentVerses` is a top-level `let` in a non-module inline script, so it lives in the global **lexical** environment and is **not** a `window` property. `window.currentVerses = …` silently creates a shadowed twin — the harness reported the reading as rendered while `.tt-word` count was 0. A **bare assignment** is the only way in, and `injectReading` now throws on a 0-word receipt rather than proceeding.

- [x] ✅ DONE S180, 1584f00 | torah_trainer.html | **"Hide nikkud" also deletes the maqaf, the sof pasuk and the paseq — welding words into nonsense on screen, in the clipboard, on the printed student handout, AND shifting the karaoke word indices** (S180 Pass H; **verified four ways with my own receipts, not an agent's**). `NIKKUD_RE = /[ְ-ׇ]/g` is U+05B0–U+05C7, which contains U+05BE maqaf, U+05C0 paseq, U+05C3 sof pasuk and U+05C6 nun hafukha — punctuation, not points. Its own comment says "nikkud only (vowels + dagesh + meteg)", and the sibling `TEAMIM_RE` (U+0591–U+05AF) correctly keeps all four, so this is a bug, not a design call. **Measured:** `stripNikkud("וַיֹּ֥אמֶר … וַֽיְהִי־אֽוֹר׃")` → `"וי֥אמר … ויהיאור"` — two words fused into one nonsense word and the verse-ending ׃ gone; reproduced by driving the real **Show nikkud** toggle, in `verseCopyText()`'s clipboard string, and — snapshotted **at print time** under `body.tt-handout-print` — on the **student handout** (`welded:true, maqaf:false, sofPasuk:false`). **The consequence the walkthrough missed:** `tokenizeHebrew` splits on `(\s+|־)` because PocketTorah counts each side of a maqaf pair as a separate sung word, and `data-twi` indexes the timings array directly — so hiding nikkud drops the sung-word count **27 → 24** (per-verse 7/14/6 → 7/12/5) and every word after the first maqaf highlights against the wrong audio timing. Fix = narrow the class to `[\u05B0-\u05BD\u05BF\u05C1\u05C2\u05C4\u05C5\u05C7]`, keeping the four punctuation codepoints; the `tokenizeHebrew` comment that documents the swallow then needs re-truing (keep the `tropeRealignFamilies` guard — it just stops firing). | found: 2026-08-02, S180 Pass H

_(**S181 Pass G** added the block below — `torah_trainer.html`'s **first-ever dedicated G** (the pointer's named target; G was stalest at S169). Run as a 4-surface parallel workflow (student handout / side-by-side parallel print / interlinear+Page-view+chrome / ink fidelity+clipboard) over **real PDFs through Chromium's print pipeline at Letter AND A4**, page counts read from the PDF bytes. **~24 findings, 7 at P2.** Every finding is print-artifact — the rubric's tie-breaker #2. **The whole set is one tool, so the variety governor caps this session at 2 of them.**)_

- [x] ✅ DONE S181, ce1eab2 | torah_trainer.html | **A4 paper silently discards every Hebrew font-size choice — the handout's three presets AND the teacher's font slider** (S181 Pass G; found INDEPENDENTLY by 3 of 4 surfaces plus my own measurement, then adversarially CONFIRMED with glyph sizes read out of the PDF content streams via PyMuPDF — not print-media emulation). `@media (max-width: 720px)` (~line 1061) is unqualified, so it applies to **print**, and its `.tt-cell.heb, .tt-heb { font-size:1.35rem }` is a literal at the same specificity as the `font-size:var(--tt-heb-size,1.5rem)` base rules (~411/616) but later in source order — so it beats both `applyFontSizes()`'s documentElement var and the handout's `body.tt-handout-size-large/-xl` body override. A4 at Chrome's default margins is 716.9–718.1px, under the 720px breakpoint; Letter at default is 740px and escapes. **Verifier widened it twice:** it fires **unconditionally** (even at the untouched 1.5rem default, A4 prints 1.35rem), and it is **width-driven, not paper-driven** — `A4@none` (794px) prints correctly while `Letter@0.5in` (720px) prints wrong, so US teachers who pick ½-inch margins are hit too. Receipts: handout large/xl = 35.2/44.8px on Letter vs **21.6px on A4**; PDF page counts Letter 2/3/5 vs A4 2/2/2. Severity corrected P1→P2 by the verifier. Page view is immune (`.tt-bible-heb` is not in the mobile rule). **Fix chosen against BOTH agents' recommendation, on measurement:** they proposed `@media screen and (max-width:720px)`; measured on paper that also hands A4 the 24px desktop `.tt-page` padding, shrinking its text column to 670px — 24px narrower than today and 22px narrower than Letter's 692px. Today's narrower mobile padding accidentally compensates for A4's narrower paper (694 vs 692). Restating the var chain inside the print block keeps that and is exactly what the file's S30 end-of-stylesheet source-order convention exists to enable.

(a) `.tt-bnum` (Page-view verse numbers) reads `var(--gold-text)`, which the dark block sets to `var(--gold)` — printing at rgb(201,146,42) = **2.75:1** instead of light #7f5a13's 6.22:1. - [~] Item (4) ✅ DONE 2026-07-29 (out-of-band, user-directed), b158af4; item (3) remains informational-only | torah_trainer.html | **Pass G print residuals** (S53). **(4) FIXED — side-by-side prints as parallel columns again.** S53 had collapsed it to one column because the two independent block flows broke at different points and produced **wrong verse pairings** (~15 verses out of sync) — truthful, but it cost the parallel text this layout exists for. Restored without the risk: in `@media print` the column wrappers become **`display:contents`** so every cell is a direct grid item, and the builder assigns each cell an **explicit `grid-row` shared across columns**, pinning a verse's Hebrew/translit/translation to the same row so they cannot drift wherever the page breaks. **The trap that made this non-trivial:** the Hebrew column also emits **aliyah dividers**, so it has more children than its siblings and any naive row-index alignment skews — the row map allocates a row per divider (spanning all columns). With no second text there is nothing to align, so that case keeps the single-column collapse rather than reserving an empty half-page. Screen is untouched (`grid-row`/`grid-column` are inert on non-grid-items; measured screen `grid-template-columns` identical before/after). **Method worth reusing: a standalone feasibility probe ran FIRST** — a throwaway page proving Chrome fragments an explicit-placement grid correctly (60 pairs, 4 pages, none split), which de-risked the whole change before a line of production code was written. Then a **negative control** (pre-fix 70/70 rows misaligned + 1 print column → post-fix 0/70 + 3 columns) and a 10-run × light/dark matrix covering 3-col, 2-col, no-parallel, interlinear and bible page; 12-page PDF generated and the rendered page inspected. **(3) still open, and still has no fix:** nikkud letter-mode colours print but collapse to similar greys on B/W — there is no secondary channel available for vowels the way the trope layer got its print underline.

  **Two maintainer decisions taken at build time:** ‹/› do BOTH (scroll between dividers on a full parsha; step the Reading picker + re-fetch on a single aliyah; aria-disabled with a stated reason elsewhere), and the bar AUTO-HIDES after 4 s idle rather than sitting permanently dimmed. **The seed's own pointer was already satisfied** — S180's `b7b7b7a` had removed the literal `font-size` from the `body.fullscreen` block, so A−/A+ move `--tt-heb-size` and work; the block's comment says never to re-add it. **Three extractions paid for ~a quarter of the diff**: `syncDarkButtons` (one loop, three carriers, replacing the same two lines copied per button across `toggleDark`+`initDark`, and guarding the header read that was unguarded); `FONT_SIZE_UI` + `setFontSize` (one slider map where there were THREE copies — `resetFontSize`, `syncFormToSettings`' `sizeMap`, the `wireSize` call list — and one writer for a size whatever drives it, clamping from the slider's own `min`/`max` so the bar can never leave the drawer's range); and `aliyahNumForLabel` lifted out of `updateJumpNavState`. **⚑ The bug verification caught, and the lesson:** stepping from `aliyahNumForLabel(_currentVerseLabel)` looked obviously right and was wrong — `jumpToAliyah` CENTRES the divider and the IntersectionObserver then reports the verse just ABOVE it (jump to aliyah 2, `_currentVerseLabel` reads `2:3`), so `›` recomputed the same target forever and could never pass the first divider. A single-press assertion would have passed; the **per-press walk of the whole cycle** (`[1,2,3,4,5,6,6,6,6]`) is what exposed it. Fixed with `fsAliyahIndexAtViewport()`, which reads the dividers' own positions — the section question, not the verse question. **Native `requestFullscreen()` WAS granted headless** (contrary to the plan's assumption), so the `fullscreenchange` listener, the Escape-exit focus rescue and the `#fsExitBtn` round-trip are covered for real, not simulated. Other notable arms: a faded bar does not intercept clicks over the reading (`elementFromPoint` returns a `.tt-word` across the strip — the `pointer-events` split is load-bearing, the wrapper spans `inset-inline:0`); zero extra Sefaria calls on a full-parsha step and exactly one per scope step; `data-twi` byte-identical across a step; `window.alert` never called; the disabled reason survives a language switch (the `applyI18n` re-assert); the bar clears `#fsExitBtn`, `.tt-jumpnav`, the karaoke bar and the hint toast at 1920 and 1280 with karaoke both on and off; `A−`/`A+` needed `dir="ltr"` on the glyphs alone (the sign is bidi-neutral and reordered to `−A` in the Hebrew UI) while the buttons still mirror.

Two conservative passes: a stroke whose every point lies within 4.5% of its own length of the chord becomes that line; an endpoint within 24 font units of a metric line or user guide moves onto it. **Three groundings made it small:** draw points are ALREADY in font units (`drawFrame` compares them to `em.descender`; `drawRenderCanvas` transforms at scale 1 + y-flip), so `collectSnapTargets()` needs no conversion; the tolerance is a CONSTANT, not `snapTolFont()` (~6 SCREEN px — the same button would do different things at different zooms, and an undoable batch action must be reproducible); and `l.drawSig` is left stale on purpose, since that is already the "strokes no longer match the traced outline" signal that re-arms Save. - **state-mutation-that-never-arms-its-persistence**: **registered + first swept 2026-08-26 (S256 Pass B) - hits: 13 setters in `Hebrew_Font_Maker.html`, all fixed (`494aa68`); 1 knowingly deferred (`setInputMode`, needs a boot guard - filed P3). clean streak: 0 - ACTIVE, and consequence-critical (data loss), so it stays ACTIVE regardless of streak.** **Definition:** a setter writes into the app's PERSISTED state object and re-renders, but never calls that app's dirty/save scheduler - so the change is real on screen, correct in memory, and gone on reload. Distinct from `debounced-persistence-with-no-page-hide-flush`: there a timer is armed and never flushed; here **nothing is ever armed**, which also silences any unsaved-work guard reading the same flag and makes an explicit flush a no-op. **Detection:** parse the file into top-level function bodies; keep those that ASSIGN into the persisted root (`project.` / `settings.`); flag any whose body lacks a call to the scheduler (`markDirty()`) or to an undo helper that calls it. Exclude the engine's own restore/undo paths, lazy initialisers, render helpers and save routines (they legitimately do not dirty). **The control is mandatory and is what makes the result trustworthy: a fresh boot must read NOT dirty.** A naive fix that dirties at load looks identical on the persistence probe and is a regression. **Placement rule:** the scheduler call goes immediately after the assignment, not at the end of the body - a setter with an early return after assigning would otherwise skip it on exactly the interesting path. **Probe note:** an inline-script `let project` is NOT on `window`, so `window.project` reads undefined and a persistence probe silently reports every value as false.
- **flex-column-crushing-its-own-rows** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-23 (S249 Pass N arm 4)**): a `display:flex; flex-direction:column` container that is ALSO height-constrained and scrollable (`max-height`/`flex:1` + `overflow-y:auto`) silently **compresses its children instead of scrolling**, because every flex item defaults to `flex-shrink:1`. The compression is not shared evenly — it lands almost entirely on whichever child has the lowest min-content floor, and if that child carries `overflow:hidden` its contents are **clipped away and become un-hittable while still reporting a sane `getComputedStyle`**. Detection: for each element whose parent is a column flex container and whose own `flex-shrink !== 0`, compare `scrollHeight` to the rendered box height; flag when the gap exceeds ~3px, and treat `overflow:hidden` on the victim as the escalation to un-operable. **Invisible to a resized desktop window** — it only fires on a viewport short enough to overflow — so it needs real device descriptors or a deliberately short window. **hits this sweep: 1 consequential (`index.html` `.ie-modal-body` → `.ivrit-mode-toggle`, 33px→2px, Automatic/Manual unreachable by finger), fixed `2453788`; clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** **Suite-wide sweep run the same session over 10 pages × iPhone SE + iPhone 13** (index, generator, dashboard, flash cards, dictionary, torah, trope, Font Maker, resources, contact): after the fix **index reports 0 clipped**, and the only other `clipped` hit anywhere is `classroom_dashboard.html`'s `span#a11yStatus`, which is **correct by design** — the textbook visually-hidden live region (`width:1px;height:1px;clip-path:inset(50%)`) — and was verified as such rather than filed. flash_cards showed 31 crushed-but-unclipped items and a dedicated collision probe found **0 actual overlaps**, so those are benign wrappers. - **legibility-destroyed-by-a-second-dimming-layer** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-23 (S248 Pass M)**): an element that is ALREADY quieted once — by a muted colour token, or by a translucent plate — is given a **group `opacity`** on top. The group opacity is the trap: it composites the element toward **whatever is behind it on the page**, not toward its own plate, so on a light surface it drags white text *lighter than the background it sits on* and muted text paler still. **The defect is invisible to a naive colour-pair check**, because `getComputedStyle(el).color` reports a perfectly good value — it only surfaces once cumulative ancestor `opacity` is composited into the foreground (exactly the probe correction S247 registered). Both of S248's contrast hits are this one shape in different clothes: `#fsExitBtn` (`opacity: 0.45` over an `rgba(13,18,32,0.55)` plate → **2.11:1** measured from pixels) and `.weather-attr` (`opacity: 0.85` over `var(--muted)` at 0.6rem → **4.35 / 4.04**). **The fix is always the same: delete the redundant layer, keep the intended one** — the plate carries the restraint, or the token does; never both. **Detection:** run the opacity-compositing contrast probe (never the naive one), then grep `opacity: 0\.` on any rule that also sets `color` or `background`. **Hits: 2, both fixed (`d31788c`, `57f379f`); clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE (consequence-critical: it is a readability class, and it re-enters any time a designer reaches for `opacity` to make something quiet).**

  _(prior)_ **swept 2026-08-17 (S224 Pass C, first run with a CORRECTLY alpha-composited detector) — hits: 2 pages fixed (`448254c`, `ed05a27`) + 1 logged, clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** Surface: 12 pages × light/dark. **Detection definition — the compositing is the whole probe.** A detector that reads the first non-transparent ancestor background reports `rgba(0,180,210,0.18)` as opaque aqua and manufactures ~27 false hits per page; the full ancestor stack must be composited before the ratio is taken. - **debounced-persistence-with-no-page-hide-flush**: **swept 2026-08-19 (S226 Pass A, 2nd sweep) — hits: 1 NEW carrier (`hebrew_dictionary.html`), fixed in-pass (`18c54ff`); the 3 known carriers re-checked and holding. clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE, and consequence-critical (data loss), so it stays ACTIVE regardless of streak.** Registered + first swept 2026-08-16 (S223 Pass B): 2 of 3 carriers hit, both fixed (`aeb7809`). **Definition:** a store written through a **debounced** timer (`clearTimeout(x); x = setTimeout(() => localStorage.setItem(…), N)`) with **no flush on page hide**, so a page discarded inside the window never runs the pending callback and the write is lost silently. **Detection (the control is mandatory):** a **pick → leave-immediately → re-read** probe run twice per carrier — dwell 0, and a dwell longer than the debounce as the CONTROL; a same-tick re-read passes on a broken carrier because the in-memory object is already correct. **Census method — SHARPENED in S226, and this is what found the new carrier:** run TWO greps and compare them as a table — a debounce-timer signature (`_*T(imer) = setTimeout` / `clearTimeout(_*save|persist)`) against a `addEventListener('pagehide'|'visibilitychange')` signature. At S226 that read FM 5/2, torah 5/2, trope 3/2, dashboard 0/2, **dictionary 1/0** — the single row where the two disagree is the hit, and it takes seconds. **S223's per-tool verdicts are NOT a safe baseline:** it cleared the dictionary on 12/12 scalar-pref round trips at dwell 0, and those prefs genuinely are synchronous — but `hebrewDictionary_lastState` is a separate writer with its own 1000 ms debounce, and probing a tool's other keys never reaches it. **Probe the key each writer owns, not the tool.** **Carriers:** `torah_trainer`, `trope_tutor`, `hebrew_dictionary` (all HIT, all fixed), `Hebrew_Font_Maker` (**the reference implementation**: `visibilitychange`(hidden) + `pagehide` → `flushAutosave()`). generator, flash cards and dashboard remain synchronous-write, verified rather than assumed. **Fix shape:** adopt the Font Maker's listener pair verbatim; `unload`/`beforeunload` are unreliable on mobile and must not be substituted. If the page's save carries a guard (torah's `_handoutActive`), the flush must carry it too.
- **async-store-backed-choice-clobbered-by-a-sync-fallback**: **swept 2026-08-19 (S226 Pass A, 2nd sweep) — CLEAN with receipts, extended past fonts as its own note directed. clean streak: 1 — ACTIVE, and consequence-critical (it destroys saved user data), so it does NOT retire on a 3-clean streak.** Registered + first swept 2026-08-16 (S222 Pass F): 3 of 6 carriers hit, all fixed (`c16c558`, `f424ea6`). **Definition:** a setting whose valid values arrive from an ASYNC store is read back by a SYNC resolver that falls back to a default for an unrecognised name — **and then writes that default back into the persisted settings**. The write-back is the defect, not the fallback. **Detection (do not weaken it):** (1) grep every `find(…) || <default>` / `? name : <default>` in a settings-restore path, then check whether the resolved value is ASSIGNED to persisted state; (2) never trust a same-tick check — pick, reload, re-read; (3) **test a store-backed value, never a built-in**; (4) check the guard AND the caller. **S226 adds rule (5), learned the hard way: a GHOST name is not a store-backed value.** An arm that seeds a name with no IndexedDB record reported **2 CLOBBERED of 5**, one of them on a page this line names as the reference implementation. The decisive arm — write a real font into `ivritsuite-fonts`, pick it through the page's own `setHebFont`, reload — **PASSES on torah, trope and dashboard**: the record resolves before any write. torah/trope normalise an unknown name to the default and dashboard/dictionary/generator leave it in place; both behaviours are safe. **Coverage beyond fonts (S226, the first time this was done):** the only two `|| <default>` resolvers outside the font pickers are read-path (dashboard `applyFontChoice`'s editor `face=` string — logged separately as a *content* consequence, not this pattern; torah's `renderText` font stack, which bails to `'serif'`), and torah's five parsha-restore sites all **bail** rather than write back. **Reference implementations:** `hebrew_dictionary.html` / `trope_tutor.html`. **Where else to look next:** any picker whose options come from IndexedDB or a `fetch` — fonts and the parsha picker are now both covered.
- **rebuild-where-a-class-swap-would-do**: **REGISTERED 2026-08-16 (S220)** — not yet swept suite-wide, hits: 1 (`26b9e7e`), clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **Definition:** a settings toggle whose visual effect is ALREADY gated in CSS on a body/root class, yet whose handler calls the page's full re-render instead of the cheap class+var swap. **Detection:** for each `settings.<flag>` written by a change handler, grep whether the flag's rendered effect is reachable through a `body.<class>` selector (or a CSS custom property) that some `apply*Colors()`-style chokepoint already toggles; if it is, a `renderText()`/`render*()` call in that handler is a hit. **Two known instances, both on `torah_trainer.html`** — the S60 nikkud layer (fixed long ago) and `colorCodeTrope` (S220). **No other tool has been checked**, and the shape is generic: any tool with a CSS-var colour layer and a master toggle can carry it. **Watch for the split that makes it safe:** an export/copy path that reads the classes off detached markup must keep its own gating, or removing the guard changes what the user pastes or prints (see `26b9e7e`'s `_inlineCopyStyles` carve-out).

- **decorative-glyph-carrier-exposed-to-assistive-tech** (**2nd instance fixed 2026-08-15, S219, c2399f1 — Font Maker QA column heads**. That instance sharpened the pattern in a way every future sweep needs: **`aria-label` on the element is NOT a fix for this class.** The FM header already had `aria-label`, so the `<th>`'s NAME was correct and a name-level check passed — but the carrier span and its text node remain in the accessibility tree beneath it (**34 dotted-circle names across 51 nodes**, → 0 across 17 after marking the span `aria-hidden`). So detection must look at the SUBTREE, not the accessible name, and must use `page.accessibility.snapshot({interestingOnly:false})` — the default prunes exactly these nodes and returns an empty set that reads as a clean pass. Second half of the S213 candidate (`templateCellHTML`) closed as NOT-APPLICABLE: it feeds `renderTemplateCanvases`, so its carrier is ink on a printed sheet, not an AT node — **a carrier inside a canvas-rasterised surface is out of scope for this pattern**.) Original definition: a glyph rendered on a **placeholder carrier character** — U+25CC DOTTED CIRCLE for an isolated combining mark — where the carrier is the only pronounceable part of the node, so assistive tech announces "dotted circle" in place of a mark it cannot voice. A **hit** requires the glyph to be a DUPLICATE: the same item's name must already be on screen adjacent to it (or on the node itself, via `aria-label`/`title`). Where the glyph IS the content (an identify-the-mark question), leaving it exposed is correct and hiding it would destroy the task — so the detection is "carrier + a sibling name", never "carrier". Detection: grep the carrier codepoint suite-wide, then ground each site by reading its builder. Swept **2026-08-15 (S213)** over `trope_tutor.html` only: **4 carrier call sites → 2 hits (fixed f207a34), 1 already correct** (`c-glyph`, whose button carries `aria-label = tropeName`), **1 correct-as-exposed** (the drill question). **Surface NOT yet covered: `Hebrew_Font_Maker.html`'s 2 visual carriers** (logged as a candidate). hits: 2, clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE

- **error-status-clobbered-by-a-later-routine-write** (**NEW, registered S199**): a status/live-region line that correctly reports a FAILURE is then overwritten, on the same code path, by a later **routine** write that assumes the happy state — so the diagnostic exists in the source, fires, and is gone before the user reads it, leaving advice that the failure itself made impossible. Sibling of `wired-then-clobbered label` (S192), but the victim is an **error message** rather than a translated label, and the clobberer is a normal-path status write rather than a JS setter. **Detection: never by reading the code** — both call sites look correct in isolation. Force the failure (block the tool's `data/` corpus with `serviceWorkers:'block'`), then read the tool's OWN `[role=status]`/live-region element at the END of init and compare it against the message the catch set. **Do NOT regex body text for `fail|error|…`** — that produced a false negative here on both carriers (curly apostrophes, and wording like "unavailable"). Swept 2026-08-12 (S199 Pass B), hits: **1** (torah_trainer, fixed b5bd9c0), clean: trope_tutor + dictionary. **Re-swept 2026-08-15 (S212 Pass B) on S199's own instruction to widen to non-init failure paths — hits: 1** (flash_cards, fixed 80695d9). **⚑ SURFACE CORRECTED: it is 5 tools, not 3.** S199 scoped the class to "the 3 tools that fetch a `data/` corpus at load" and wrote off "the other 4" — but flash_cards and the generator fetch `data/hebrew_words.json` **lazily**, so they carry the class and sat outside the declared surface for 13 sessions. Flash cards was the hit; the generator is clean **because it already had the fix** (`_realWordsFailed`), which is where the flash-cards patch was copied from. Clobberer definition widened too: not only an end-of-init routine write but **any later routine re-render**, of which a language switch is the cheapest universal trigger (`applyI18n` re-renders every page's JS-built content). Clean this sweep: dictionary, torah_trainer, trope_tutor, generator. **Detection, both traps now recorded: do NOT regex body prose** — S199's regex produced a false NEGATIVE (curly apostrophes, "unavailable"), and S212's produced three false POSITIVES by being English-only across a language switch. Read the specific element, and make the re-render probe language-agnostic (switch EN→HE→EN, so a merely TRANSLATED message returns while a destroyed one stays gone). Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.
- **animation-outside-its-reduced-motion-block** (**NEW, registered S198**): a CSS `transition`/`animation` declaration whose selector is **not covered by its own page's `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block** — so a reader who asked the OS for less motion still gets that one. CLAUDE.md makes the coverage binding ("if you add an animation to a page, that page needs the reduced-motion block, and your animation must honor it"), which is exactly why a *partial* block is the dangerous shape: the block's presence reads as compliance. **Detection (cheap, mechanical, no rendering needed):** for each file, collect every selector carrying a `transition:`/`animation:` declaration outside the reduced-motion block, then subtract the selectors named inside it; anything left is a candidate. **Confirm at runtime with a control arm** — read `transitionDuration` under `reducedMotion:'reduce'` **and** `'no-preference'`; a probe that reports `0s` in both states is measuring nothing. **The sibling heuristic is what found S198's hit:** elements that *travel together* (a drawer and its backdrop, a modal and its scrim) must be neutralized together, and a block naming one but not the other is the tell. Swept 2026-08-12 (S198): **1 hit / 3 carriers of the settings drawer** — `torah_trainer` (fixed 915526d); `classroom_dashboard` and `trope_tutor` already correct. **Not yet swept suite-wide** — S198 censused only the `.settings-backdrop` shape; the full 11-page selector-subtraction sweep is the next A run's job. ACTIVE, clean streak 0. **⚑ FIRST GENERAL SWEEP 2026-08-12 (S199): 4 hits, all fixed (6fcf9e4).** Surface: all 12 pages, current-state. **Detection is now settled, and two thresholds must be right or the number is meaningless:** run the page under `reducedMotion:'reduce'` and read COMPUTED `transition-duration`/`animation-*` — but (a) **`0.00001s` is the neutralizer idiom (`0.01ms !important`) and counts as COVERAGE, not a hit**, so threshold at >1ms, and (b) bucket by transitioned **property**: explicit `transform`/position/size (and any keyframe animation) is the defect; a hover **colour/opacity** fade is not, and lumping them in inflates ~16 real hits to ~108. Result: keyframe animations already neutralized on **every** page (0 suite-wide); the escapees were 4 explicit `transform` transitions on 4 pages (`404 .home-btn`, `generator .vg-arrow`, `dashboard .day-item`, `dictionary #fsBtn`), each on a page whose block already existed and simply omitted them. **Fix-shape note: `!important` is usually REQUIRED, not stylistic** — a media query adds no specificity, so an equal-specificity rule declared later in the file wins (404's fix parsed fine and did nothing until it was added), and `.vg-arrow` carries its transition as an **inline** style. Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **Remaining, deliberately NOT claimed as defects:** the `transition: all` hover declarations on generator/dashboard/dictionary/torah (see Candidates). **S204 detection refinement: the census MUST include bare-duration shorthands — `transition: 0.2s` is implicit `all` and a literal-'all' grep misses it (3 of torah's 8 real sites were this shape, one hiding the toggle-knob translateX, the class's first real motion hit). transition:all arm status after S204: dictionary S203 + generator/torah S204 CLOSED; dashboard is the last arm.** **S205: the transition:all backlog candidate is fully CLOSED (all four arms + flash_cards clean by census); the PATTERN stays ACTIVE for new code.**
- **content-dependent-tour-step-miscounts-the-tour** (**NEW, registered S197**): a guided-tour step whose `target()` only exists once remote/corpus content has rendered. The engines all skip an unresolvable step **silently by design** ("skip gracefully when hidden"), but the step counter is built from the **raw array index**, so on any failed/absent load the number **jumps and over-promises** — the teacher watches steps vanish. **Detection (cheap, ~2 min/tool): walk the real tour on a fresh profile and compare steps SHOWN against `TOUR_STEPS.length`; then re-walk with that tool's own corpus route-aborted.** The second arm is what makes it discriminating — the first arm alone only catches tools whose content is EXTERNAL (torah/Sefaria), and silently passes every tool served from local `data/`. **Fix shape: count by PRESENCE of each target, never visibility** — absent = content never arrived; hidden = a collapsed panel that opens fine. Presence is also the only side-effect-free probe: testing visibility means running every step's `reveal()`, which in the dictionary opens the sidebar and expands panels the tour hasn't reached. FIRST sweep 2026-08-12 (S197 Pass I), all 7 tour-bearing tools: **2 carriers found, both fixed → 0 remaining** (`torah_trainer.html`, `hebrew_dictionary.html`). **trope_tutor is the documented NEGATIVE — it has a content-dependent step too (`#tuCards .tu-card`) yet holds 6/6 with data blocked**, which is what proves the detector isn't just reporting "blocking data breaks tours". The other 4 tools target static chrome only. **Clean streak: 0 (first sweep, hits found).** ACTIVE.
- **per-sample-repaint-of-an-O(n)-live-preview** (**NEW, registered S196**): a continuous gesture — `pointermove`, a slider drag — that rebuilds an **O(n) preview from its whole accumulated buffer once per input SAMPLE** rather than once per animation frame, so the gesture is O(n²) in its own length. The screen cannot show more than one repaint per frame, so every extra rebuild is pure waste, and the cost is invisible at the short strokes/small drags a developer tests with. **Detection:** find the expensive builder call inside a `pointermove`/`oninput` handler where the builder walks a whole array; then, under **PACED** input (yield to rAF between batches — a synchronous dispatch loop starves rAF and fakes a 100× win), count builder invocations against frames. A per-sample handler shows `invocations == accepted samples`; a correct one shows `invocations ≈ frames`. Confirm with a first-10%-vs-last-10% mean ratio per sample — a flat ratio is clean, a rising one is the class. **Fix idiom (already in-tree twice):** `boldGenSet` and `nodeStatusCoords` — coalesce with an rAF token on the gesture object, re-read state at frame time (never snapshot), and guard the callback with `gesture !== g` so an ended gesture paints nothing. **Found + fixed 2026-08-12 (S196, Pass D): 1 hit** — Font Maker's four styled draw pens (2e09c29); its round pen is the same shape but measured under budget and deliberately left (logged as a Candidate with the two inputs that would make it actionable). **⚑ Notable: S85's Pass D fixed this exact shape in the same tool** (Generate Bold's per-frame warning scan), and Draw mode reintroduced it 111 sessions later — so this class recurs *within* a tool as new gesture surfaces are built. Clean streak: 0 (first sweep). Correctness-adjacent (degrades the primary drawing interaction), not consequence-critical.
- **false-positive-validator-on-the-app's-own-content** (**NEW, registered S194**): a QA/lint/warning rule whose **detector is broader than the failure it warns about**, so it fires on artwork or data the app itself ships — the user cannot act on it, cannot clear it, and it is present in **every** project, which is precisely how a panel of real warnings gets trained into background noise. Founding instance: the Font Maker outline scan flagging its own built-in **Comma** and **Semicolon** (`glyphOutlineScan` tested "do two contours' edges cross" while the message promised "can fill **inverted**" — inversion needs *opposite* winding, and both glyphs are all-outer, so nonzero simply unions them). **Detection:** for each validator, run it on a **pristine/empty project** — anything it reports there is by definition not the user's doing. Cheap (one page-evaluate) and it generalizes past contrast/i18n to every warning surface: FM QA, the export guard, the dictionary/flash-cards load states. **Second question once a hit is found:** is the right fix to *exempt the built-in* or to *narrow the detector*? Narrowing is usually correct and fixes the class — but check the narrowing does not silently drop a real case (here, "windings differ" would have missed hole/hole double-subtraction, so the rule became "skip only when BOTH are outer"). swept 2026-08-11 **S194**, hits: 1, clean streak: 0 — **ACTIVE**

- **wired-then-clobbered label** (NEW, registered S192): an element that carries a **correct `data-i18n` binding** and is then **overwritten by a JS setter with a hardcoded English literal** — so `applyStaticI18n` translates it and the setter immediately reverts it. Distinct from `pre-ready-i18n / never-re-rendered` (a builder that runs before `I18n.ready` and is never re-run): here the key IS referenced and the wiring IS correct; a later writer clobbers it. **Why both gates are blind to it:** the literals characteristically sit in a **ternary** (`c ? 'Edit kern class' : 'New kern class'`) or an **array** rather than a plain assignment, which is exactly Check A's documented blind spot; and Check B only measures CSV translation coverage, which is complete. **Detection (repeatable, cheap):** build a map of `id → data-i18n key` from the file's static markup, then scan every `.textContent`/`.innerHTML`/`.value`/`.placeholder` assignment whose RHS contains an English string literal and no `I18n.t(`, resolving the target element by the nearest preceding `getElementById` within ~12 lines. **Triage rule learned on the first run:** that ID-proximity heuristic mismatches — 2 of 4 raw candidates were the generator's printed worksheet subtitles attributed to an unrelated `worksheet.layout.title_aria` binding, and printed output is never-translate anyway, so **always confirm the resolved element really is the bound one before logging**. **Fix shape:** retarget the binding as well as the text (`setAttribute('data-i18n', k)` + `textContent = I18n.t(k)`) — the existing suite idiom at `flash_cards.html` `timerShowLabel`. That is what makes a language switch land, and it avoids the trap of "just add the function to `applyI18n`", which is **illegal** when the function mutates state (`applyI18n` must stay read-only). Guard the text write against the pre-ready case (`t()` returns the key before locales load) so a raw dot-key can never be painted. Swept 2026-08-11 (S192, first sweep): **4 raw / 2 real / 2 fixed / 0 left**, across all 13 root HTML files. Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.
- **theme-flipping-token-on-a-fixed-colour-plate** (NEW, registered S191): a control or text node styled with a colour token that **inverts with the theme** — `var(--text)`, `var(--white)`, `var(--muted)` — placed inside a container painted a **fixed** colour that does not invert (a `--navy`/`--navy-deep` plate, a gold button, a print sheet). One theme composites fine and the other collapses toward 1:1, so a single-theme check clears it and the failure lands in whichever theme the author was not looking at. **This is the documented `--white` pitfall in CLAUDE.md read in the other direction** — that note warns `var(--white)` text disappears on navy in DARK; the S191 hit was `var(--text)` disappearing on navy in **LIGHT** (the bulk dock's `.btn-secondary`, measured 1:1, label rendered as an empty box). **Detection is not greppable** — the token and the plate are in different rules — so it needs the alpha-compositing contrast probe run in **both** themes, with transparent backgrounds walked up to an opaque ancestor. The house fix is the existing navy-plate idiom: literal `#fff` on `rgba(255,255,255,0.12)`. **Consequence-critical (a control whose label is invisible), so it does not retire on a clean streak.** — ACTIVE **2nd sweep 2026-08-11 (S193 Pass A): 1 hit, fixed (cd52e15).** Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **Definition widened: the class has a MIRROR IMAGE** — S191's was an inverting token on a fixed plate; trope_tutor's is a **fixed** colour (the UA default `#0000EE` on an anchor no rule reached) on a plate that **inverts**. Same failure and same 1–2:1 floor, opposite cause; the compositing detector finds both because it measures the result, not the tokens. That makes **3 carriers in 4 sessions** (torah_trainer dock, trope_tutor About, FM hints) and confirms the detector's value: it is one page-evaluate, needs no compositing baseline, and the misses are always anchors the page simply never styled because a `footer a`/`.panel a` rule did not reach them. **Next carriers to sweep: the 5 dormant anchors the S193 run found un-rendered** — enable each one's disclosure state first, which is exactly what turned the FM hint links from "never measured" into a confirmed 1.81:1. **Re-swept 2026-08-12 (S199) via the UA-default-anchor sub-detector, with every disclosure FORCED OPEN so the dormant carriers render: 1 hit (index `.ie-note a`, 1.63:1 dark, fixed 071e326) + 1 REFUTED.** That closes the "5 dormant anchors" queue and the count reconciles exactly: 3 FM hint links (S194) + these 2. **Standing false positive, do not re-chase:** `hebrew_dictionary .skip-results` reads 1.81:1 in dark but only while clipped to 1×1px offscreen; its only visible state is `:focus`, which sets `background:var(--navy); color:#fff`. **A forced-open detector must be paired with a real-state confirmation** — the index hit was re-measured with the gear modal genuinely opened before it was logged. **S202 hit (the mirror image again): the FM wizard modal's `.tbtn.ghost` — a fixed navy-toolbar token (gold-light) on the theme-flipping modal plate — 1.5:1 in light on the gate's only exit; fixed 3a33b1a by rescoping the file's own `.tour-card` repair. - **two-state-ready-flag-for-a-three-state-load** (NEW, registered S189): a lazily-fetched corpus or module whose UI decides what to render from a single truthiness check — `REAL_WORDS.length`, `EMOJI_DATA`, `_wordsReady`. **That flag has two states; the fetch has three** (never attempted / in flight / failed), so the "not ready" arm is also what a FAILED load renders, permanently: either a confident false zero ("0 matching words" — worse than silence, because it is a claim about the user's own selection) or a "Loading…" that never ends, refreshed by every later re-render and language switch. **Detection:** for each lazy fetch, name its ready flag, grep every render that branches on it, and ask what the failure path leaves on screen; then stall the resource AND 502 it headless, reading the end state **after ≥4 s** — a short sample cannot tell "stuck" from "not yet". **Run both languages:** the dictionary instance PASSED in English and FAILED in Hebrew, because the later locale fetch changes whether a re-render lands after the catch. - print-media-leak / var-chain-overridden-by-a-literal: **2nd instance found + fixed 2026-08-02 (S182)** — `.tt-grid{align-items:start}`, correct on screen (the grid items are the 3 column wrappers) but wrong in print, where `display:contents` promotes every CELL to a grid item and the row border then draws at 2–3 different heights. Generalises the pattern: it is not only `@media (max-width:N)` blocks leaking to paper, but **any screen-correct declaration whose meaning changes because print restructures the box tree**. Still swept on `torah_trainer.html` only.
- print-media-leak / var-chain-overridden-by-a-literal: **registered + first swept 2026-08-02 (S181 Pass G)** over `torah_trainer.html`'s full stylesheet. 3 `@media (max-width:…)` blocks (600/900/**720**px); the 720px one was unqualified and reached paper. Method that found it: computing printable content width per paper×margin instead of assuming print is wide — A4@default = 718px < 720px while Letter@default = 740px, so **it is width-driven, not paper-driven** (`A4@none` 794px prints correctly; `Letter@0.5in` 720px prints wrong). **The other 11 root pages have NOT been swept for this** — do it in the next A.

- **S165 (2026-07-27): `pre-ready-i18n / never-re-rendered` hit a 3rd time, and the test harness itself was found unsound for failure paths.** Pass F swept failure behaviour across all seven tools: the dictionary's parse-time fetch threw a ReferenceError in its own `.catch` (deferred `js/i18n.js`), and torah_trainer's empty state showed raw keys because `applyI18n` re-rendered the reading only when one was loaded. **Two sub-lessons worth keeping.** (1) Healing a stuck key from the *visible text* is a half-fix — the line then stops following language switches; record the key at write time and re-resolve from it. (2) **Service workers defeat `page.route`**: `sw.js` uses `skipWaiting()`+`clients.claim()`, so `/data/` comes from `DATA_CACHE` and never reaches the route handler. Any offline/failure test must open the context with `serviceWorkers: 'block'`; without it the test reports the happy path while appearing to test failure. This manufactured a "Flash Cards is silent" finding that the maintainer then chose at gate 1 — caught before any code was written, by instrumenting the writes instead of trusting the observation. **Every previous route-abort-based "offline" result in this ledger should be treated as unverified for the same reason.**

**⚑ Out-of-band (2026-08-22, maintainer skill update to `.claude/skills/improveloop/SKILL.md`; ledger rotation row added alongside; no code, no sw.js bump — non-precached files only; session counter untouched):** the loop protocol gained **pass N — mobile & touch-device** (the maintainer's ask: "add a pass for mobile support… with screenshots and decision gates like other passes"). One surface per session, on **real device emulation, never a resized desktop window** — the recipe delta is binding because a Playwright *device descriptor* is what flips `(pointer: coarse)`/`(hover: none)` to true and sets `maxTouchPoints`/DPR (measured at registration: `devices['iPhone 13']` → coarse `true`, hover-none `true`, dpr 3, maxTouchPoints 1; a plain 390px-wide desktop context → `false/false/1/0`), so a resize-only run silently misses every hover-only and coarse-pointer finding. Seven arms: reflow/overflow at 320/390/412 + landscape × both themes × EN **and** HE; the viewport & zoom contract (three viewport-meta spellings across the 14 root HTML files today; `user-scalable`/`maximum-scale` clean, kept as the control; `viewport-fit=cover` ↔ `env(safe-area-inset-*)` pairing — only `flash_cards.html` carries either, and it has both); dynamic browser chrome (**13 pages use `100vh`, 0 use `dvh`/`svh`** — and headless CANNOT measure it, `visualViewport.height === innerHeight` with no collapsing URL bar, so it is audited statically per use site); touch-only interaction parity (hover-reveal, DnD-only paths, finger-draggable sliders, the tooltip tap contract under `hasTouch` — only 3 root files carry any touch handler today, so *absence* is the expected finding); on-screen-keyboard ergonomics (`inputmode`/`type`, `autocapitalize`/`autocorrect`, focused-field survival under a ~45% keyboard, `prompt()` flows tapped through); standalone/PWA reality (no browser back button on a home-screen install → dead-end hunt, safe-area, orientation flip); and one throttled phone-performance arm (4× CPU + slow network) that hands anything deeper to D. **Boundaries written into the definition:** C keeps a11y semantics *and* the WCAG 2.5.8 touch-target SIZE rule with its registered `sub-floor touch target` pattern (N never re-files a size finding — it files reachability/operability ones); M keeps visual refinement; B/I keep the load-time gates at narrow widths (both already run 375px load arms); G keeps paper. New **decision gate 4** (mobile restructuring & desktop-affecting mobile fixes): a change scoped inside a phone-width media query stays autonomous, but anything that changes what DESKTOP users see, restructures/reorders/**hides** content at phone widths, adds a touch-only gesture or a phone-specific warning/blocking screen (incl. declaring a surface desktop-only — the FM `mobileWarnDismissed` notice is the one precedent, not a licence for more), or migrates units/breakpoints page-wide (`100vh`→`dvh`) is proposed with current-state phone screenshots and ASKED; unattended default = don't ship, log the proposal as a Candidate with its screenshot paths. **Screenshot rule is stricter than M's:** every N run ships a **phone contact sheet even when it finds nothing** (each audited page full-page at the portrait width(s) run, light + dark, EN + HE) plus BEFORE/AFTER pairs for every fix — scratchpad only, never committed, delivered at close-out; "it's fine on a phone" is a claim the maintainer must be able to SEE. Fixes verify at the phone width(s) found **plus** the standard desktop/800 matrix, and extend an existing phone media query rather than inventing a breakpoint (**42 distinct `max-width` values already, 35 under 1000px** — measured at registration).
