**Method notes new in S224:**
(1) **Five candidate findings this session were probe defects, and every one was caught by a control or a re-measurement — none by inspection.** 27 light-mode contrast "misses" (detector read `rgba(...,0.18)` as opaque instead of compositing the ancestor stack → true figure 0); 3 dark "misses" on buttons that are `disabled` and WCAG-exempt; a tour dialog that "did not restore focus" (the probe never focused the trigger before clicking it, so there was nothing to restore); a "nameless" Sefaria link (the detector did not follow name-from-content into a descendant `img[alt]`; Chromium's own `ariaSnapshot()` reports `link "Sefaria"`); and a whole-suite 0/0/0 sweep that was really a dead HTTP server. **The S223 tell held every time: a result too catastrophic or too uniform to be real.**
(2) **A silent `catch { continue }` in a sweep turns an outage into a clean bill of health.** The suite-wide run reported all 12 pages perfect with 0 errors because `page.goto` was failing and being swallowed. **Assert `resp.ok()` and throw** — a sweep that cannot distinguish "nothing wrong" from "nothing measured" is worse than no sweep, because it produces a receipt.
(3) **A source grep is not a detector for anything whose fix can live on another line.** Grepping `classList.toggle('active'` named 12 unexposed selector groups on the generator; a runtime check found all 12 correctly expose `aria-pressed`, written elsewhere. The two real hits were on pages the grep-based reading had not even suggested. **Measure the rendered state, then use the grep to locate the writer.**
(4) **When a WCAG census looks enormous, the exceptions are the finding.** 52 sub-30px controls sounds like a systemic failure and is actually zero: 30 clear the 24px spacing exception, 9 are inline prose links, 1 is a ledgered exemption. **Encode 2.5.8's spacing exception in the probe** (a 24px circle centred on each target that must not reach another target's centre) or the census is unusable.
(5) **A documented constant can be exactly right about its own arithmetic and still be the wrong constant.** The dashboard's `0.30` ink-flip threshold came with a comment correctly deriving it as white's 3:1 large-text crossing — the derivation was sound, the *bar* was wrong, because the text it governs renders at 21.6px/500 and WCAG large text starts at 24px. **Check which bar applies before checking whether the value meets it.**
(6) **Third session running, the fix was already authored elsewhere in the repo.** The generator supplied `aria-pressed` mirroring for S224's chrome fix and `body.dark .vowel-chip-sub{color:#adb6c9}` for the dictionary's. **When a sweep shows one tool passing and others failing, read the passing one first** — it yields a better fix and a better comment than deriving one (S222 method note 3, now with two more instances).
(7) **A verification that fails on its first run is doing its job — and so is one whose assertion is wrong.** The `aria-pressed` fix shipped 15 unseeded pills until verification caught them; the reflow fix "failed" 4 of 10 cells purely because the expected desktop width omitted a 1px border. **Distinguish a failing fix from a failing assertion before touching the code**, and settle "did I regress desktop?" with a stashed clean tree rather than arithmetic (361.0 → 361.0).

**Method notes new in S223:**
(1) **Three of this session's first four "findings" were probe defects, and the tell was always the same — a result too uniform or too catastrophic to be real.** 0/13 pages failing the language switch (the switcher is a `<select>`; the probe looked for a `button`), a Font Maker throw (`_selectItem('letter', 0x05D0)` — `project.letters` is ARRAY-indexed, so a codepoint was passed where an index belongs), a generator throw (`generateWorksheet` for `generate()`). **A whole-suite failure is far more often a whole-suite probe bug than a whole-suite regression** — S211 said a clean result deserves a second look and S222 extended it to apparent regressions; extend it now to *unanimous* failures.
(2) **The corollary, and the one that mattered most: a probe defect can be hiding a REAL defect at the same address.** The panel-memory arm reported torah and trope failing; the focused re-run with a control passed 3/3 and looked like a clean acquittal. The difference was **timing, not state** — the passing probe happened to dwell ~300 ms longer — and chasing *that* is what found the unflushed save debounce. **When a re-run acquits, diff the two probes and explain the delta before closing the finding.**
(3) **A persistence probe needs a dwell contrast, not just a reload.** Same-tick re-reads pass (the in-memory object is correct) and slow probes pass (the debounce fired). Only "act → leave immediately → reload" fails, and only against a "act → wait → leave → reload" control does that failure mean anything. This is now written into the new pattern's detection definition.
(4) **An overflow census is worthless without an off-canvas exclusion filter, and the filter is what overturned a 10-session-old attribution.** S213 concluded three of four pages did NOT attribute to `.hright` because "their widest boxes sit inside the off-canvas settings drawer" — the drawer was being *measured as page content*. Walking each ancestor and discarding `position:fixed` + non-zero `translateX` (and any hidden ancestor) turned four mysteries into one shared cause. **Any geometry census on a page with a drawer needs this filter before its "worst offender" list means anything.**
(5) **When a previous session proves a lever inert, the useful question is what ELSE could move that constraint — not whether they were wrong.** S218 correctly established `flex-wrap` cannot beat `flex-shrink:0`, and framed the remaining work as "establish what `flex-shrink:0` is protecting" — a question that leads toward removing a protective flag. `max-width:100%` makes the flag irrelevant instead: it caps the container so wrapping engages, and the protection stays. **A blocked fix is sometimes blocked only at the lever the last attempt reached for.**
(6) **Test a CSS rule unscoped before choosing a breakpoint — inertness is measurable, and it differed per file.** The identical rule was fully inert above 412px on trope and flash_cards but shifted the dictionary's header at 390–1024px. Measuring that across nine widths turned "pick a breakpoint" from a guess into a per-file decision with evidence, and is what let two of the three files avoid a magic number entirely.

**Method notes new in S222:**
(1) **A consistency probe must include a CONTROL arm whose value takes a different code path.** Running the My Fonts contract with a built-in font alongside a stored one is what turned "three tools are broken" into "one *value class* is broken in three tools" — built-ins persisted 6/6, My Fonts 3/6. Without the control the finding would have been mis-scoped as three unrelated per-tool bugs, and the shared class (and its reference implementation) would have been missed.
(2) **A guard on the setter is worthless if the caller coerced the value first.** Flash Cards' `applySettings` normalised an unknown font id to the default *before* `refreshMyFonts` could match it, so the same one-line guard that fixed torah_trainer measured **no change at all** there until the upstream coercion went too. When fixing a "restore the saved value" bug, follow the value from storage to the setter and check every rewrite on the way.
(3) **The fix for a cross-tool divergence is often already authored in the repo — go and read the tools that pass.** `trope_tutor.html` carried the exact guard, comment and rationale, and trope's shell was *copied from* torah_trainer; the guard simply never travelled back. Diffing the passing carrier against the failing one produced a better fix (and a better comment) than deriving one would have.
(4) **A probe that dismisses "open modals" must enumerate every backdrop class, not the one it remembers.** Clearing `.overlay.open, .fr-modal.open` left the first-run `.fr-backdrop.open` (z-index 600) covering the week editor (561), so `elementFromPoint` returned the backdrop and the drag-paint gesture measured as painting only its origin cell. This is the **second** time a stale first-run card has manufactured a false finding on the dashboard (S211 was the first) — treat `.fr-backdrop` as part of the standard dismissal sweep.
(5) **When a fix appears to regress something, suspect the measurement before reverting.** The "torah now renders Hebrew in a Latin sans" reading came from measuring `#ttReading`, a container, rather than a Hebrew leaf; the computed `--heb-font` was Frank Ruhl Libre all along, identical to the two reference tools. S211's corollary — a clean result and a lone-laggard result both deserve a second look — now extends to apparent regressions.
(6) **Verify "pre-existing vs. caused by me" with a stashed clean tree, not by reading the diff.** The weekly grid's non-byte-identical `.ivrit` round trip (`v:2`→`v:1`, `weekend:false` injected) looked alarming mid-verification; re-running the same probe on a stashed tree settled it in one minute. Run the stash check from the repo root — a shell cwd left in the scratchpad makes `git stash pop` fail with exit 128 (S221 hit this twice).

**Method notes new in S221:**
(1) **`page.pdf({format})` silently overrides the page's own `@page size`.** Playwright applies its `format` option unless `preferCSSPageSize: true` is passed — so a page that hardcodes the wrong paper and a page that declares the right one produce **identical** PDFs, and the probe reports the defect fixed either way. This nearly discredited a correct S219 measurement: the first run showed control and fix matching and looked like evidence S219 had been wrong. Any test of what an `@page` rule *declares* must pass `preferCSSPageSize: true`; a test of how content *paginates* on a given paper should not.
(2) **A key census built from literal greps is systematically incomplete, and the missing keys are the interesting ones.** `setItem('literal'` found 36 of 51; the 15 it missed were the 6 folder trees, the 3 panel-memory keys and the Font-Maker constants — i.e. exactly the shared-block and newest-feature keys most likely to be under-reconciled. Resolve every `setItem(CONST` through its declaration before claiming a storage sweep is complete.
(3) **An exemption is only trustworthy once you have read what the key actually holds.** `hebrewFontMaker_recentProjects` and `hebrewFontMaker_uiPrefs` are indistinguishable from their names and their absence from the erase list; opening them split the pair decisively — one stores 6 complete project payloads (correctly preserved), the other 19 UI fields that all have inline defaults (wrongly preserved). Name-level reasoning would have produced either a missed defect or a data-loss bug.
(4) **A boot-write census is a cheap, whole-suite reconciliation probe** — wrap `Storage.prototype.setItem`/`removeItem` and `indexedDB.open` in an `addInitScript` and load every page on a fresh context. It answers "what does this app write before the user does anything?" in one run, needs no interaction scripting, and gives a receipt that is meaningful even when clean (14 keys, all reconciled). Worth re-running whenever a tool gains persistent state.
(5) **When a state-setup helper refuses silently, the receipt must be in the same `evaluate` as the setup.** `_certEnter` early-returns unless a profile has passed all ladder levels, so two consecutive bad seedings produced fully-formed PDFs that measured plausibly and proved nothing. Returning `{active, rule}` from the same evaluate call caught it immediately — and the second bad seeding was caused by trusting a `grep -A 8` that truncated a 12-entry table at 8.

**Method notes new in S220:**
(1) **A poll that breaks on "queue is empty" must first wait for the queue to become non-empty.** The chunked-build probe polled `_wsBuildQueue.length === 0` immediately after clicking Generate, before the click handler had populated it — so it broke on the *previous* render's empty queue and reported **36 sheets for a 40-version build**. The build was fine; the probe read a start state as an end state. Any "wait until done" poll on a queue, a flag or a spinner needs a "wait until started" phase first, or it measures the wrong edge.
(2) **When a probe reports a functional failure inside a PERFORMANCE pass, suspect the probe's timing first.** Both of S220's kills were the same settle window: 1,200 ms was enough for ten drills and not for crossword, so crossword alone reported "0 sheets, 2 elements" — indistinguishable from a real defect until it was re-run with a longer wait and the generator was timed directly. **Time the function, then time the interaction**: `generateCrossword` at 3–8 ms against a 2.5 s paint is the pair of numbers that settles it, and neither number alone would have.
(3) **Split a block into its parts before proposing a fix, or you will optimise the wrong 6 %.** The bingo block looked like an obvious O(cards × pool) shuffle problem, and the shuffle *is* wasteful (48 ms, and a partial Fisher-Yates would be 8 ms) — but a detached-DOM microbench put the whole 200×25-cell build at 60 ms, which means ~85 % of the 834 ms was live style+layout that no JS change touches. **The candidate is worth more than the fix would have been**, and it says so explicitly so the next D does not re-derive it.
(4) **A helper that supplies a fallback `aria-label` will silently take the accessible name away from an element that already had one.** `bindTip` sets "More information" only `if (!wrap.getAttribute('aria-label'))` — perfect for a bare `?` icon, wrong for a chip whose visible text *is* its name. Setting the label before binding is a one-line precaution that has to be taken deliberately, because nothing fails and no gate catches it; the name is simply wrong to a screen reader.
(5) **Grounding a stale candidate is not wasted work — it is where the live instance was found.** The S209 anchors-banner candidate had been fixed for ~10 sessions and never ticked. Opening the function to fix it showed the fix already in place *and* an untranslated sibling one branch below, in the `else` fallback. **Always read the whole function a stale candidate points at**, and tick the stale line so the next session does not repeat the trip.
(6) **`page.emulateMedia({media:'print'})` does NOT fire `beforeprint`.** The print band measured 0 chips under print emulation and looked like a regression; calling `buildPrintBand()` explicitly returned the expected 6. Anything populated in a `beforeprint` handler has to be invoked by hand under `emulateMedia`, or its emptiness proves nothing.

**Method notes new in S219:**
(1) **A print measurement taken at zero margins is not a print measurement.** `page.pdf()` defaults to `margin: 0`, and at margin 0 the S219 card-sheet defect measured **16/16 clean**; at the 1in margin the code's own comment budgets for, the same matrix measured **16/16 broken**. Always sweep the margin (0.25in → 1.25in) and report the largest margin at which the artifact still paginates correctly — that number is a far better regression anchor than a single page count.
(2) **`page.pdf()` fires `afterprint`, so it destroys any artifact torn down on that event.** All three flash-cards print modes wipe their host in an `afterprint` listener, so the first run's twelve "clean" A4 sheets were 1 KB empty documents rendered after the Letter pass had already torn the artifact down. Re-fire the artifact before EVERY `pdf()` call, and treat a suspiciously small PDF as evidence of this rather than of a clean page.
(3) **`page.accessibility.snapshot()` prunes the exact nodes the decorative-carrier pattern lives in.** The default `interestingOnly:true` returned `[]`, and a `dotted.length === 0` assertion PASSED on an empty set. With `interestingOnly:false` the same tree showed 34 dotted-circle names across 51 nodes. **Assert the snapshot is non-empty before trusting any zero drawn from it** — this is the S218 "a probe that manipulates state must verify the manipulation landed" rule, extended to probes that merely *read*: verify the read returned something.
(4) **`aria-label` fixes an element's NAME, not its subtree.** A decorative glyph span inside a correctly-`aria-label`led `<th>` stays in the accessibility tree and is still met by a reader browsing content. Name-level checks pass; subtree-level checks do not. Any future sweep of this pattern must walk the subtree.
(5) **Driving app state by assigning globals skips the sync functions that make the state real.** Setting `otherSubMode='words'` directly bypassed `syncOtherSubUI()` and produced a false zero that looked like a defect; driving the actual pills produced the true behaviour — which turned out to be a *different*, real defect. Drive the UI the user drives.
**Method notes new in S218:**
(1) **A reveal probe must assert that the reveal SUCCEEDED before its verdict means anything.** The probe reported "STALE-FOREVER (English survives reveal)" for two findings while printing `visible after: false` in the same block — the reveal never fired, so the verdict was a claim the action had not earned. Both findings survived, but on *other* evidence (a hardcoded English data table; a raw call beside three `_pT` siblings). This is the S217 hidden-DOM trap wearing a different hat: there the probe read hidden DOM and called it visible, here it failed to reveal and called it stale. **The general rule: a probe that manipulates state must verify the manipulation landed, in the same breath as reporting the result.**
(2) **The detector can UNDER-measure, and a control is what reveals it.** Pass K reported 2 hits in the Font Maker; the fix actually repaired **10 tiles**, because Yiddish and Specialized render an "enable this tab" hint instead of tiles in a fresh profile, so 8 names were never in the DOM to be detected. Driving the real `setAdd*` setters exposed them. **A runtime detector measures the default state, not the reachable state** — for optional/behind-a-flag surfaces, drive the flags before believing the count.
(3) **When a raw value has a translated twin one line away, the twin is both the proof AND the design.** Both shipped fixes were found the same way and fixed the same way: the era badge beside `${w.pos}`, the three `.lt-name` siblings beside `precompName(pc)`. The twin proves it is chrome rather than content (someone already decided), and it hands you the exact mechanism (`I18n.t` mapping with a raw fallback; `gName`). Third session running for this shape — S177, S211, now S218.
(4) **Read the mapping out of the markup that already holds it, instead of duplicating it.** The dictionary fix could have hardcoded a 20-entry `pos → key` table; instead `posLabel()` scrapes the filter panel's own `value` / `data-i18n` pairs. The badge then *cannot* disagree with the filter that produced the result, and a future filter row wires its badge for free — the duplication would have been a fresh divergence of exactly the kind the fix was repairing.
(5) **`flex-wrap` is inert against `flex-shrink:0`.** A container that never shrinks below its max-content width never runs out of room, so its children never wrap. The reverted iteration-5 attempt spent itself learning this; the entry now says so, which is worth more to the next attempt than the failed diff would have been.
(6) **Check whether a "1px under" measurement belongs to the instance or to its class.** `#tourBtn` at 66×29 looked like one button; `.hbtn` turned out to be a shared class of five whose `≤720px` padding trim was the real cause. Measuring **all five across seven cells** — rather than fixing the one instance the walkthrough named — is what turned a patch into a floor, and it also proved the change was a no-op for the other four (their dimensions are byte-identical pre and post).
(7) **A gate answer can close a question permanently, and that closure has to be written down where the detector will look.** The flash-cards colour labels are a deliberate non-defect now, but the reverse-lookup detector will resurface those 13 strings on every future K. The CLOSED-BY-DECISION candidate exists so the next session recognises them as answered rather than re-deriving the whole analysis.

**Method notes new in S217:**
(1) **Four kills, one cause: the probe looked in the wrong place and reported the page's silence as the product's.** Every one of Pass H's would-be findings was "X fails silently", and every one died the same way — the handling existed, in a different element than the probe queried (`#ttStatus` not `#ttReading`; `.tt-notice-chip` not a toast; `.tt-translation` not `.tt-en`). **"No message found" is a claim about the selector, never about the product**, and the cheap discipline that catches it is to read the failure path in the source *before* writing the assertion, then assert on the element that path actually writes.
(2) **A stub that omits a field the app validates manufactures a defect out of the app working correctly.** The Sefaria stub's version entries had no `license`, so `isPermissiveLicense` rejected them and the translation never rendered — read as "translation is broken" when it was the copyright safeguard doing its job. A stub must satisfy every guard on the path it stands in for; the tell here was that the *guard* was reachable in the source and the fixture had no field to feed it.
(3) **`display:none` on a parent does not make children compute to `none` — a visibility helper must be ancestor-aware.** The print check used a per-element `getComputedStyle(e).display !== 'none'` filter and reported speak buttons inking on the student handout; `el.checkVisibility({checkOpacity:true, checkVisibilityCSS:true})` shows print fully clean. **This is the same trap the S207 K-pass already documented**, which is the real point: a documented trap recurred because the helper was rewritten from scratch rather than copied from the pass that had already solved it.
(4) **`emulateMedia({media:'print'})` does not fire `beforeprint`.** The print band was "absent" until the event was dispatched manually — the band is built by `buildPrintBand()` in the `beforeprint` handler, so media emulation alone tests a page state no real Ctrl+P ever produces. Emulate the media **and** dispatch the event.
(5) **Not every lead is a finding, and saying so is the finding.** The chant-all audio behaviour looked like a dead-end, but three candidate causes — headless autoplay policy, route interception, real product behaviour — could not be separated, and `audio.error` stayed `null` even on a 403. **S165's fabricated "silent on failure" finding is the precedent**: it came from exactly this shape. Logging it as an unresolved lead *with the method notes for separating the causes* is worth more than either a fix or a silence.
(6) **A candidate that demands attribution can have more than one cause, and closing one does not close the candidate.** The S213 reflow entry said "attribute before changing anything"; attribution found **two** independent contributors. Fixing the torah-specific one is a real fix and the page still overflows at 320 on the other. Re-measure **per cause**, and say in the ledger which half shipped — otherwise the next session reads a fixed commit against an open candidate and cannot tell whether the entry is stale or the fix failed.
(7) **An interrupted loop loses its memory, not its work.** S217's commits survived (a check-in caught two of them unpushed in an ephemeral container and pushed them); what nearly did not survive was **everything above** — four kills, an attribution, and a lead, all of which existed only in conversation. The close-out is not paperwork appended to the session; it *is* the session's durable output, and it should be written before the budget is spent, not after.

**Method notes new in S216:**
(1) **Produce the artifact and LOOK at it — the style assertions were 99/99 green on a sheet that was scrambled.** The micro-feature passed every visibility, computed-style and colour check while printing a week whose times sat mid-row and whose classes sat under the wrong days: hiding the row-delete button removed a **grid item**, so each row slid one track left. No property was wrong; the *geometry* was. The assertion that catches this class is **column and row alignment** (every time-cell shares one x, every day's cells share one x, every period's cells share one y) — added, and verified against a control that re-introduces the old rule. Two further defects came out of the same look: a blank second page from `body{min-height:100vh}` (100vh IS one sheet on paper) and a 4 s cleanup timer short enough to undress the sheet mid-render.
(2) **`page.pdf()` only defaults to print media if `emulateMedia` was NEVER called.** This probe emulated `screen` earlier in the same loop to check the editor recovered, and that stuck — so the first four "artifacts" inspected were the **dashboard in screen media**, two pages of cream background, and were read as evidence about the sheet. The tell was chemical, not logical: the fills in the PDF were the dashboard's auto-assigned preset palette, not the fixture's three colours. **Assert the artifact is the artifact** — the fix was to check that the fixture's exact colours appear in the decompressed content streams, which also catches the next silent substitution.
(3) **The corpus is part of the measurement, and `<head>` is the wrong one on this codebase.** Two parity tables contradicted each other about whether torah_trainer claims print; the loser was the one that sliced everything before `</head>`, which on that page is 88,641 chars of mostly `<style>` and scored 62 `print` hits from CSS comments and a `media="print"` preload. Crawler-facing copy is exactly `<title>`, the `content=` of description/og:*/twitter:*, and the ld+json bodies. Per S215's note: the self-contradiction was the proof, and it cost one command to resolve.
(4) **A detector that returns "0 problems" must also report how many cases it could DECIDE.** The forward claims-vs-UI arm reported 0 unreferenced controls out of 83 claims — and 0 of those 83 were decidable, because these FAQ bodies are prose with no quoted control names. The number that mattered was the one not being printed. (Same run, a second instance: `git ls-tree -- '*.html'` returns nothing at root, so the byte check's first cut announced "0 pages changed of 0".) S215 said every probe that can return a zero needs a case it is known to catch; **S216 adds the cheaper habit — print the decidable denominator, and a vacuous clean announces itself.**
(5) **Re-read a recurring pattern's own rule AFTER fixing it, not just before.** The JSON-LD parity line carries an explicit S190 warning that every claim on these pages has a visible on-page twin and that a one-sided fix creates a new mismatch. The fix was written from the *finding* rather than from the *rule*, moved the JSON-LD from 7 Questions to 8, and left the `<details>` FAQ at 7 — re-opening the pattern in the act of closing it, and it was caught only when the close-out went back to update the pattern's health line. A pattern's rule is a post-condition as much as a detector.
(6) **Look at the distribution before calling a threshold a defect.** The pass definition says titles should run ~50–60 chars; privacy and terms measure 27 and 25 and are correct, because the suite's own titles run min 25 / max 61 / median 51 and the short ones are all brand or legal pages. The same probe's description arm WAS a real finding by exactly the same test — 92 and 99 against a 136–164 band with no other page under 110. One number is a threshold someone chose; twelve numbers are evidence.

**Method notes new in S215:**
(1) **The blind-zero trap bites CHECKERS, not just pages.** S214 established that a page returning 0 under `reduce` proves nothing without a reduce-off control. S215 hit the same shape one level up: four shared-block probes returned "0 carriers, single-sha" — a *clean-looking* result produced by a regex that could not match anything, because those blocks' start markers are multi-line comments and the anchor required a same-line `*/`. A checker that finds nothing and a checker that cannot find anything are indistinguishable from the output alone. **Every probe that can return a zero needs a case it is known to catch** — here, the fix was to print the carrier LIST and the per-block sha, not just the verdict, so an empty list is visible as an empty list.
(2) **When a checker contradicts documentation, suspect the checker first — and when it contradicts ITSELF, that is proof.** Three of four hits died this way. The tell that saved the most time was self-contradiction: D10 reported 378 files missing while the manifest and the directory both looked healthy, which (exactly as S200 recorded for its 204-missing-AND-258-orphan case) means a wrong naming assumption rather than a broken corpus. Grounding cost one command each; logging any of them would have cost a future session an investigation.
(3) **A documented provenance stamp is not a checkable claim unless its method is recorded.** CLAUDE.md stamps the panel-collapse block `sha-verified 2026-08-15: b58130835987`. Twelve slice×algorithm variants (inner/with-markers/raw/stripped × sha256/sha1/md5) failed to reproduce it, so the stamp cannot be used to detect drift — while the property it exists to assert (all 6 carriers byte-identical) IS independently verifiable and holds. Recorded as informational, not as a hit: **you cannot call drift on a number you cannot recompute.** If future stamps are meant to be checkable, they need their slice definition written beside them.

**Method notes new in S214:**
(1) **For a COVERAGE-shaped pattern, the delta method under-measures by an order of magnitude — measure current state.** The reduce signature found 29 new motion declarations in the delta; grounding those alone would have produced a handful of fixes and a "clean-ish" verdict. The runtime measurement found **1,286** live animations, because the defect is the absence of coverage for declarations added across many prior sessions, not the new lines. Delta-scoping is right for "did this change introduce a sink?" and wrong for "does this page's guard still cover the page?"
(2) **A zero and a zero are not the same result — check the control per page, not per suite.** privacy.html and terms.html returned 0 animating under `reduce`, which looks identical to flash_cards' 0. Their reduce-OFF control also returned 0: there is no motion to neutralize, so the page proves nothing. The per-page control is what separates "honours the setting" from "has nothing to honour", and without it a sweep banks two free passes it did not earn.
(3) **The specificity argument is the whole safety case for adopting a universal `!important` rule — so assert it, don't reason it.** `*, *::before, *::after` at (0,0,0) cannot beat `.pulse-attn` at (0,1,0), which is why the bespoke *static replacement cues* survive. That is a two-line argument and it is also exactly the kind of thing that is wrong in practice; re-asserting all six replacement cues under `reduce` after the change (ring ×4, inset ring, tint) turned it from an argument into 6/6.
(4) **`0.001ms`, not `0`, and the reason is a real dependency.** A zero-duration animation does not fire `animationend`; the generator's shuffle cells remove their class from that event, so a `0` neutralizer would have left `.shuffling` stuck on every cell. The in-repo block already used `0.001ms` — copying it verbatim inherited a decision that would have been easy to "simplify" into a bug.
(5) **A key census that does not know the file's key-BUILDING helpers reports confident nonsense.** The first i18n pass reported 24 unauthored keys across 9 files; every one was the literal prefix of an `I18n.t('fontmaker.qa.tab_' + id)` concatenation. Tightening the regex to require the closing quote be followed by `)` or `,` took it to 2,947 references and 0 misses — and the one remaining "miss" is `i18n-test.html`'s deliberate `this.key.does.not.exist`. The S209 note predicted this exactly; it is worth re-reading before any census, not after.
(6) **An exclusion is a finding and deserves the same evidence as a hit.** The FM printed tracing template builds `'◌' + base` beside a visible name — textbook shape for the carrier class. It is not a hit because `renderTemplateCanvases` rasterises that HTML through html2canvas and it never enters the accessibility tree. Recording *why* it was excluded costs one line and stops the next sweep from "fixing" it.
(7) **Ship the gate answer that was given, not the proposal that preceded it.** S212's candidate proposed converging the four registers AND dropping the generator's duplicate message. The maintainer's recorded answer covered the wording only. Executing the extra clause would have removed a user-visible message on an unasked authority — the diff was one line shorter and the decision was not mine.

**Method notes new in S213:**
(1) **A differential against a sibling file is the cheapest possible proof, and it also tells you what "fixed" should look like.** The skip-link defect was not diagnosed by reasoning about `<main>` focusability — it was measured by running the SAME probe against `torah_trainer.html`, whose skip target already carries `tabindex="-1"`. That produced the before/after receipt (`focusMoved` false→true) and, separately, settled the only real objection to the fix: the UA focus ring the target now shows is not a new artifact, because the twin has shown it all along. When a suite is built from copied shells, the twin is the specification.
(2) **A live-region test that counts MutationObserver CALLBACKS always passes.** Observer callbacks are delivered in a microtask, so a synchronous read of a counter is 0 whether or not the DOM changed — the "3 no-op re-renders wrote 0 times" check was passing blind until its own control (a deliberate write, also counted as 0) exposed it. `mo.takeRecords()` is synchronous and is what such a check must use. This is the S211 "clean sweep is the more dangerous result" lesson recurring in a new disguise: the control is what made a green check mean something.
(3) **"Still exposed" is a vacuous pass on an element that is not there.** The control proving the drill question's glyph was NOT wrongly hidden ran against an Identify question — whose stem renders a marked word and has no glyph tile at all — so it reported `exists=false, aria-hidden=null → still exposed ✓`. Any assertion of the form "X does not have property P" must first assert that X exists. Re-run against Hear/Melody it became a real check.
(4) **Measure the accessibility tree, not the DOM, when the claim is about what a screen reader says.** `page.accessibility.snapshot({interestingOnly:false})` turned "screen readers probably announce the carrier" into 10 nodes before and 0 after, with trope-name nodes held at 36 as a negative control. It is one call, it needs no extra tooling, and it is far harder to argue with than a reading of the markup.
(5) **A finding measured across the suite is not a one-tool fix — and an unattributed cause is not a fix at all.** The 320px reflow miss reproduces on 4 of 5 pages, so it belongs to pass F/G, not to a C session's one-tool budget. More importantly, the detector's "widest box" list is NOT the cause on 3 of those 4 pages (the widest boxes sit inside the off-canvas drawer and exceed the measured scrollWidth), so it was logged with the attribution explicitly marked as unfinished rather than shipped as a guess.
(6) **When the maintainer picks a copy-bearing option at gate 1, draft the copy and ask ONE focused question with the real strings.** Showing three concretely-worded alternatives got a decision in a single round; asking "what should it say?" would have cost a round trip and produced a worse answer.

**Method notes new in S212:**
(1) **A clean sweep must be shown capable of failing, and the control has to break the RIGHT thing.** The 56/56 corrupt-storage result was only worth reporting because a control run made it fail — but the *first* control was malformed (it corrupted the whole script block, so the page died for the wrong reason and `panelMemSave` was undefined, which the receipt exposed). A control that fails for an unintended reason proves nothing except that the page can break. Replace exactly the one construct under test — here `ivritSafeParse`+guard → bare `JSON.parse` — and confirm the *shape* of the failure matches the hypothesis (1 of 8 shapes, the malformed-JSON one).
(2) **A recorded detection warning can have a second edge — read it as a class, not an instance.** S199 wrote "do NOT regex body text" after a regex produced a false NEGATIVE (curly apostrophes, "unavailable"). S212 used a regex anyway, in a different way, and got three false POSITIVES: an English-only pattern cannot match a correctly-translated Hebrew notice. Same root cause — measuring prose instead of the element. Where a probe must survive a language change, make it language-agnostic by construction: round-trip **EN→HE→EN**, so a merely translated message comes back and a destroyed one stays gone.
(3) **Inherited surface definitions expire; re-derive them from the code.** The `error-status-clobbered` pattern carried "surface = the 3 tools that fetch a `data/` corpus at load" for 13 sessions. One grep for `fetch('data/` showed **5** — flash_cards and the generator fetch lazily, so "at load" quietly excluded them, and the class's 2nd hit had been sitting in one of them the whole time. When a pattern line states its own surface, spend the one command to re-verify it before trusting the exclusion.
(4) **A blocked external dependency does not have to mean an unexercised code path — stub it.** Torah's render pipeline needs a Sefaria response, and the standard recipe aborts every external origin, so previous B runs could only watch it fail. Fulfilling the Sefaria route with a small synthetic v3 payload ran the real pipeline offline (21 words, trope + nikkud colour, dark, HE) and exercised the S211 hot-path early-returns that were the whole reason B was picked. Reusable for any tool whose main path is behind a third-party fetch.
(5) **Report the iteration that found nothing.** The last iteration chased the generator's caption and concluded the code was correct — no commit. That is a real result (it closed a suspicion and produced an INFO candidate so the next pass does not re-derive it), and recording it honestly is what keeps the pass-hit-rate statistics meaningful.

**Method notes new in S211:**
(1) **A consistency probe deserves the same scepticism as a bug report — in BOTH directions.** Pass F's three self-caught defects split as one false FAILURE (a laggard that was a fixture artifact) and one false CLEAN SWEEP (12/12 passes from a check that compared a value to itself). The clean sweep is the more dangerous of the two, because nothing about it invites a second look. Before believing any all-clean consistency result, ask what the probe would have to do to FAIL.
(2) **A toggle test must toggle an ODD number of times.** Exercising Enter and then Space to prove both work leaves the widget exactly where it started — so any downstream persistence/reload assertion silently compares a value to itself and passes everywhere. Separate the "both keys work" check from the "state survives" check.
(3) **A debounced save and a `page.reload()` are a race the reload wins.** torah's `saveSettings` is a 300 ms `setTimeout`, and navigating cancels the pending timer, so a persistence probe that reloads immediately reports "resets" for code that works perfectly. Wait past the debounce (grep the save function for its delay first) before any reload-based persistence check.
(4) **Assert the MECHANISM, not just the outcome.** The dashboard contrast fix's first cut used a 0.4 luminance cutoff and changed nothing at all — `#c8a000` sits at 0.373. It was caught in one run only because the probe printed the `ink-dark` CLASS alongside the ratio; a ratio-only probe would have shown "still 2.48" with no clue whether the rule was wrong, the class unapplied, or the selector mis-specified. When a fix has a trigger and an effect, measure both.
(5) **Prefer thresholds that are derived, not chosen.** Replacing that 0.4 with 0.30 was not tuning: white text scores (1.05)/(L+0.05), which crosses the 3:1 large-text bar at exactly L=0.30. A derived constant can be defended in a comment, survives someone adding an eighth day colour, and does not need re-tuning when the palette moves.
(6) **When a candidate says "re-derive before assuming", do exactly that — and be willing to close it.** The dashboard's six-taps-seven-cells receipt did not reproduce, and grounding showed all three mechanisms that could have produced it (`paintCell` idempotence, `addWeekPeriod`'s null push, `sortWeekPeriods` permuting cells with periods) are individually clean. Closing a stale finding with a receipt is a real iteration outcome, not a wasted one.
**Method notes new in S210:**
(1) **An EN-vs-HE rendered-body-length ratio is a cheap whole-page localization detector.** It needs no key census, catches an entire page in one measurement, and distinguishes untranslated-vs-content-only by counting Hebrew-bearing blocks. terms.html's 6199→6198 (a ONE-character delta, against privacy.html's 7199→6112) is what surfaced the finding.
(2) **`data-i18n` coverage is not translation coverage.** terms.html carries 35 `data-i18n` attributes and passes every structural check; the defect lived entirely in the CSV's empty `he` cells, which Check B reports **warn-only**. A green i18n gate is not evidence a page speaks Hebrew.
(3) **A selector that names the thing can still match the wrong thing.** `.legend` matched the *grid* legend ("image/traced/anchored") rather than `#stageLegend`, manufacturing four confident false passes — the S209 distinctive-substring lesson recurring. Prefer the id the render function itself writes to (locate it by reading the function, not by guessing the class).
(4) **Stub the timing, not the outcome, when proving a render-count fix.** The translit differential only held because the stub ESM carried a *controllable import delay*: with an instant stub, both baseline and fixed render once and the bug is invisible. Fulfil the CDN with a delay, and run the slow case too — that is what proves the fallback path survived.
(5) **When a candidate's every slice needs new copy, an unattended gate makes it unpickable.** The torah failed-reading dead end (P3, reproduced live by this pass) had to be passed over for its non-copy sibling; prefer logic-shaped candidates in unattended sessions and save copy-shaped ones for the gate batch.
**Queued and needing no gate:** (1) the **FM backlog's last 3 keys** — letter_drop/markctl_drop need the 2 kind keys ("an SVG"/"an image"), side_positions_kept needs the .one/.other transcription of the live possessive ternary (no new wording; HE drafts REVIEW-marked); (2) the **NEW S209 P4** — the anchors-preview banner literal (needs 1 authored key); (3) the dictionary font-license nested-interactive span (the haul's one deliberately-parked item).
**Gate queue for the next attended batch:** the two S180 splits — the parsha **deferred-fetch flow** (P3, gate-2: changes the pick-a-parsha default) and the **font-panel/size-slider cross-reference** (P4, gate-2: wording/IA). **Gate-1 lead unchanged: the dashboard weekly-grid print seed** (offered twice, skipped twice, never struck). **Maintainer review queue: 3 REVIEW-marked HE drafts** (flashcards.sheet.practiced/_tip S207, fontmaker.status.template_saved S208).
**Method notes new in S209:**
(1) **A regex census cannot see helper-CONSTRUCTED keys.** The fresh RFC-4180 census flagged the 5 anchor_* keys as unwired because anchorLabelT builds `'fontmaker.panels.anchor_' + slug` at runtime — a literal-argument regex sees nothing. Cross-check every "unwired" hit against the file's known key-building helpers (the ledger's dynamic-reachable list was already right); the 2 kern_export_summary plurals are the same lesson dot-side.
(2) **The FM wizard fixture defaults trop OFF, and gotoAnchors('trop') falls back to nikkud silently** — call setMarkEnabled('trop', true) first, and remember the anchor-panel hints render only with an ACTIVE mark (click one in the grid). Also the workspace left panel is `#ctlLeft` (.ws-left) — a `.ws-side` selector silently falls through to body-text matching, where substring collisions (vowel vs trop hint texts) manufacture false passes; match on DISTINCTIVE substrings.
(3) **Verify BOTH state signals on rebuilt DOM.** The chant button's template carried state-true TEXT but dropped the .active CLASS on every fetchAndRender rebuild — a class-only probe read "not engaged" while the user-visible label was correct. When a button's state renders in two channels (label + class), assert both; fixing the template to render both is the durable shape.
(4) **A "N small ones" polish-set candidate can hide gated members** — ground each item before treating the set as one mechanical iteration: of the S180 four, one was already resolved (stale), one was mechanical, and two were gate-2 (default-flow and wording changes). Splitting them into their own gated candidate lines keeps the set honest.
**Method notes new in S208:**
(1) **PDF geometry receipts need a CTM walker + /Pages /Kids order.** Raw `Tm`/`re` operands sit under per-block `cm` transforms (Chromium prints at a 3.125× internal scale with per-run translations), file-scan `/Type /Page` order is NOT reading order, and content streams carry **clip-culled neighbour-page text** that a naive above-content-top filter counts as band content (the walker proved it: page 1 = exactly the band's 12 runs; pages 2+ = those 12 + 8 culled body runs). This **retroactively qualifies the S207 band-rect receipt** — right conclusion, but its y-filter happened to match device-space rects; future print receipts walk the CTM, order pages by /Kids, and window to the band's own geometric strip.
(2) **Choose fixture parshiot so the aliyah starts fall inside the fixture's refs.** parshaSelect index 1 is Noach (starts 6:9+ — zero matches against a chapters-1/2 fixture, so 0 dividers render and a divider-dependent receipt silently degrades); index 0 Bereshit puts 2:4/2:20 inside a two-chapter [120,80] fixture. S207's verify_band used Noach harmlessly (no divider dependency) — divider staging is what exposed it.
(3) **One remapped token can converge a whole dark-accent leak class.** Before adding per-selector print re-inks for `body.dark` rules, check whether every PRINTABLE reader of the token wants the same paper value — `--gold-light`'s only background uses were :hover states, so print-remapping the token itself (→ text-gold) fixed nn-val, the holiday line, omer, weather-temp, and text links in one line.
(4) **The dense-sidebar visibility-wait class recurred** (S202/S207's note holds): `<option>`s and collapsed-panel content need `state:'attached'`, and a dynamically-rendered error affordance can hang off a DIFFERENT ancestor than its happy-path sibling (the weather ↺ Refresh lives under `#weatherBody`, not `#weatherBlock`) — hide-list selectors must target the common ancestor.
**Method notes new in S207:**
(1) **The parent-only computed-style visibility filter is ancestor-blind** — `getComputedStyle(child).display` does NOT inherit an ancestor's `display:none`, so every "visible" hit must be re-proven by rect area / `checkVisibility()`. But the blind arm is worth running deliberately: hidden-DOM English finds stale boot renders and closed-modal unwired strings that a strict-visible collector (S192) provably missed. Run BOTH arms, then a reveal probe to split stale-forever (real) from rebuilt-on-reveal (benign).
(2) **A render-once guard defeats applyI18n's re-render coverage** (`if (grid) renderGrid(); else renderPanel()`): the panel half keeps its build-time language forever while the key census counts it "wired". Sweep i18n-bearing builders for once-guards; the fix is an explicit full rebuild in applyI18n with the form-reset trade documented in place.
(3) **position:fixed + an enlarged @page top margin = a per-sheet running header that cannot overlap content** — verifiable without pdftotext by decompressing PDF content streams (object-boundary splitting, then slice by the declared `/Length` — `rstrip` can eat a trailing 0x0A that is REAL deflate data) and counting the band's ops above the content-top y on every page.
(4) **`waitForSelector` needs `state:'attached'` for `<option>`s and collapsed-panel content** (hit twice this session — the S202 visibility-wait class keeps recurring).
**Method notes new in S206:**
(1) **fixed-position overlays have offsetParent === null.** An offsetParent-based visibility filter silently drops every open modal — three of this pass's four false alarms trace to that one probe shape. Filter on getComputedStyle position + display instead.
(2) **Ground a dead-end candidate against the button's render path before converting its alert.** The queued weakness alert() was unreachable (the render hard-disables the button); the real fix was disabled→aria-disabled + a stated inline reason — the Start-button shape the file itself documents.
(3) **The ?s= emit side can reuse the paste-code encoder byte-for-byte** — emit the URL-safe alphabet the decoder already tolerates and the link path adds zero new parsing surface (and the words-inline embed travels for free).
